subject: Conference: Inference Summit — discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Conference: Inference Summit — quick follow-up

Hi Samir —

Great meeting you at the Inference Summit yesterday. I enjoyed our quick chat about FinTechX's latency-sensitive fraud scoring pipeline and the challenges you mentioned around peak-hour token costs and model version consistency across environments.

If you're open, I'd love to set up a 30-minute discovery call next week so we can:
- Understand traffic patterns (qps / burst) and peak latency SLOs
- Walk through current model variants and deployment setup
- Share how Redwood tackles cost (batching/caching/quantization) while preserving quality

Mateo (cc'd) is our solutions lead and would join to answer infra questions. Are you available Tue 4/6 11:00am PT or Wed 4/7 2:00pm PT? I can send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan after the call.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0133

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conference: Inference Summit — quick follow-up

Hi Marissa —

Great to meet you too — apologies for the delayed reply, the team has been heads-down on end-of-quarter. Tue 4/6 11:00am PT works for me. I'll invite Jamie (ML infra) as well. High level context for the discovery: we run a retraining+serving loop for our fraud model; during spikes we sometimes push a cheaper quantized variant but see occasional regressions. Latency SLO is <120ms p95; token costs are a growing line item.

Talk Tuesday — thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Engineering, FinTechX
samir.patel@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conference: Inference Summit — quick follow-up

Thanks — confirmed for Tue 4/6 11:00am PT. Invite attached.

To help us prepare, could you share two things before the call if convenient:
1) A high-level traffic pattern (peak rps and typical seq lengths) or a short perf summary from your monitoring dashboard
2) Any existing evaluation set you use to measure quality/regressions when you switch quantization profiles

I'll put together a 15-minute agenda and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) we can iterate on. Looking forward to the chat.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechx.com>, Jamie Nguyen <jamie.nguyen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Conference: Inference Summit — discovery recap + MAP

Hi Samir / Jamie —

Thanks again for your time on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Meeting summary:
- Primary use case: real-time fraud scoring pipeline with p95 latency target <120ms and heavy burst traffic during promotional events.
- Current pain points: cost pressure during peaks, occasional quality regressions with quantized variants, and a fragmented deployment story across cloud regions.
- Goals: reduce token/instance cost by 20-30% without degrading p95 latency or model accuracy; standardize deployment across regions; define rollout policy for quantized variants.

Proposed MAP (attached): MAP_FinTechX_20270406.pdf
- Week 1: Redwood runs a short eval on a representative eval set (you to share) and a traffic profile (you to share).
- Week 2: Pilot on a non-prod subset with batching + prefix caching + quantization profile A; measure p95 and accuracy delta.
- Week 3: Expand pilot, iterate; plan canary rollout and rollback thresholds.

Next steps assigned:
- Samir / Jamie: share eval set & traffic summary (ideally by 4/9)
- Marissa / Mateo / Ben: run initial eval and share recommendations (deliverable by 4/13)

I've attached the MAP and included a short checklist for the pilot. Let me know if the timeline is too aggressive; happy to adjust.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: MAP_FinTechX_20270406.pdf

Just circling back on the MAP I sent last week — wanted to check if the timeline is still reasonable and whether sharing the eval set / traffic snapshot for Week 1 is still on track.

If priorities have shifted, no problem — can you let me know a more realistic date? If helpful, we can also compress the initial eval (shorter dataset + focused metrics) to get preliminary recommendations faster.

If I don't hear back, I can try a quick ping next week — wanted to avoid dropping this while the promotional season ramps up.

Thanks,
